## 1 · What could AI do for me?

<p class="lead">Start from work you already do, not from a tool. Use three questions (Activities, Actors, Artefacts) as a thinking aid, not a form to fill in.</p>

```{=html}
<div class="split">
  <div class="card"><span class="ct">Good candidates</span>
    <ul>
      <li><b>Recurring</b>: every month, every survey round, every mission</li>
      <li><b>Same steps</b> each time</li>
      <li>An <b>output you can check</b> in minutes</li>
      <li><b>Data you may share</b> with the tool</li>
    </ul>
    <span style="color:var(--grey)">Keep for yourself: judgment calls, relationships, sign-off. "Not here" is a valid answer.</span>
  </div>
  <div class="card line"><span class="ct">Think each one through</span>
    <div class="a3mini">
      <b>Activities</b><span>What are the steps?</span>
      <b class="g2">Actors</b><span>Which steps need me? Which could run without me?</span>
      <b class="g3">Artefacts</b><span>What would the tool see, and what would it hand back for me to check?</span>
    </div>
    <span class="opt" style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:flex-start"><span><b>Optional:</b> map one workflow fully as a matrix. It takes longer than today, so start it now and finish it with your agent later.</span><a class="zm-link" href="#/anatomy-of-a-workflow-matrix-answering-a-ministry-data-request">See an example matrix →</a></span>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="lookup">Look up: <a href="#/activities-actors-artefacts">Activities, Actors, Artefacts</a><a href="#/three-workflows-redesigned">Three workflows, redesigned</a><a href="#/anatomy-of-a-workflow-matrix-answering-a-ministry-data-request">A workflow matrix, step by step</a><a href="#/example-an-ai-data-map">An AI data map</a><a href="#/example-an-ai-data-map-for-a-dashboard">A dashboard data map</a></div>
```

::: {.notes}
Time: 3 minutes. Activities, Actors, Artefacts is a thinking aid here, not a deliverable. For each candidate task, three quick questions: what are the steps, which need me, and what would the tool see and hand back. Steps that do not need you and end in something checkable are where an agent fits.

A full workflow matrix is optional. It usually takes longer than the 30 minutes, so encourage people to start one and finish it with their agent after the session.

If the room needs a concrete example, jump to "Three workflows, redesigned" in the reference section (monthly welfare nowcast, stakeholder presentation, survey cleaning), then come back.
:::

## Redesign it one stage at a time

```{=html}
<div class="qs">
  <div class="card"><span class="num">1</span><span class="q">Does this stage need my judgment?</span><span>No: it can happen without you. Yes: keep it, but let the agent prepare it.</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="num">2</span><span class="q">What does the agent hand back?</span><span>An artefact you can check in minutes: a memo, a diff, a flag list. No artefact, no handoff.</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="num">3</span><span class="q">What starts it?</span><span>You asking in a chat, a colleague's request, a file arriving, a date. Name it, so everyone knows when the handoff happens.</span></div>
</div>
<div class="chain">
  <div class="st ai"><b>Pull &amp; check</b><small>agent, when you ask</small></div>
  <div class="ho"><span>memo</span><i>→</i></div>
  <div class="st you"><b>Decide</b><small>you</small></div>
  <div class="ho"><span>assumptions</span><i>→</i></div>
  <div class="st ai"><b>Run</b><small>agent, after your sign-off</small></div>
  <div class="ho"><span>tables</span><i>→</i></div>
  <div class="st you"><b>Interpret</b><small>you, with the agent</small></div>
  <div class="ho"><span>draft</span><i>→</i></div>
  <div class="st ai" style="border-style:solid;border-color:var(--rule);color:var(--grey)"><b>Clear</b><small>reviewers</small></div>
</div>
<p class="keep">Keep for yourself: <b>decisions</b>, <b>relationships</b>, <b>sign-off</b>. Everything between them is a candidate for the agent.</p>
```

::: {.notes}
Time: 2 minutes. Ask these three questions of each step in a candidate task. Most Bank workflows start with someone asking, in a chat or by email, and that is fine. The point of question 3 is to name the handoff, not to automate it.

The chain at the bottom is the monthly welfare nowcast from the reference section, in five steps.
:::

## 2 · What do I need to do, and what is in the way?

<p class="lead">Sort your next steps by how ready they are. The examples are illustrations, not a checklist for everyone.</p>

```{=html}
<div class="cards c4 hz">
  <div class="card"><span class="n">THIS WEEK</span><span class="ct">Now</span><span class="q">Already works, low risk</span>
    <span class="eg">e.g. the agent on one recurring task in your real work</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="n">NEXT 6 WEEKS</span><span class="ct">Set up</span><span class="q">Needs some setup or team agreement</span>
    <span class="eg">e.g. a de-identified or synthetic version of sensitive data</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="n">NEXT 3 MONTHS</span><span class="ct">Define</span><span class="q">Not plug-and-play yet. Start defining the need now</span>
    <span class="eg">e.g. a review routine for the team's outputs</span></div>
  <div class="card road"><span class="n">CANNOT SOLVE ALONE</span><span class="ct">Roadblocks</span><span class="q">Write them down anyway</span>
    <span class="eg">e.g. a data agreement that may not allow it, tool access, a skill that does not exist yet</span></div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note-custom}
For most teams the biggest step is a **de-identified or synthetic version of sensitive data**, so the agent can work on the real pipeline. Public data can stay in your project folder as it is.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lookup">Look up: <a href="#/plan-your-tasks">Plan your tasks</a><a href="#/sensitive-data">Prepare sensitive data</a><a href="#/skills">Skills</a><a href="#/who-needs-access-and-to-what">Team access</a><a href="#/risks-and-how-to-reduce-them">Risks</a></div>
```

::: {.notes}
Time: 3 minutes. Stress that the examples are illustrations: people should write targets that fit their own work. "Use AI more" is not a target. "Every change to the cleaning code gets an AI review before merge" is.

Roadblocks are the most useful output of this session for us. Encourage people to write down the worry even if it is vague, for example "not sure our data agreement allows this". Missing skills go here too: we do not expect people to build their own yet.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var REF = ['activities-actors-artefacts', 'anatomy-of-a-workflow-matrix-answering-a-ministry-data-request', 'three-workflows-redesigned',
    'example-an-ai-data-map', 'example-an-ai-data-map-for-a-dashboard', 'what-did-you-set-up-this-week-check-those-that-applied', 'plan-your-tasks',
    'skills', 'who-needs-access-and-to-what', 'sensitive-data', 'risks-and-how-to-reduce-them'];
  var OVERVIEW = 'what-to-look-up-and-when';
  var zm, frame, title, target, backBtn;

  function build() {
    var slides = document.querySelector('.reveal .slides');
    zm = document.createElement('div');
    zm.className = 'zm';
    zm.innerHTML = '<div class="zm-panel"><div class="zm-view"><div class="zm-frame"></div></div>' +
      '<div class="zm-bar"><span class="zm-t"></span><button class="zm-btn" data-a="close">Close</button>' +
      '<button class="zm-btn go" data-a="go">Go to slide →</button></div></div>';
    slides.appendChild(zm);
    frame = zm.querySelector('.zm-frame');
    title = zm.querySelector('.zm-t');
    zm.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
      var a = e.target.getAttribute && e.target.getAttribute('data-a');
      if (a === 'go') { go(target); }
      else if (a === 'close' || e.target === zm) { close(); }
    });
    backBtn = document.createElement('button');
    backBtn.className = 'ref-back';
    backBtn.textContent = '← Back to overview';
    backBtn.addEventListener('click', function () { go(OVERVIEW); });
    document.querySelector('.reveal').appendChild(backBtn);
  }

  function open(id) {
    var sec = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!sec) return;
    target = id;
    var c = sec.cloneNode(true);
    c.querySelectorAll('aside.notes, .notes, .mk, script').forEach(function (n) { n.remove(); });
    c.querySelectorAll('[id]').forEach(function (n) { n.removeAttribute('id'); });
    c.querySelectorAll('.fragment').forEach(function (n) { n.classList.remove('fragment', 'visible', 'current-fragment'); });
    frame.className = 'zm-frame' + (sec.classList.contains('smaller') ? ' smaller' : '');
    frame.innerHTML = '';
    while (c.firstChild) frame.appendChild(c.firstChild);
    var h = sec.querySelector('h2');
    title.textContent = h ? h.textContent : '';
    zm.classList.add('open');
  }
  function close() { zm.classList.remove('open'); }
  function go(id) {
    close();
    var sec = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!sec) return;
    var i = Reveal.getIndices(sec);
    Reveal.slide(i.h, i.v, -1);
  }

  // keep the arrow keys from moving the deck while the preview is open
  document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if (!zm || !zm.classList.contains('open')) return;
    if (e.key === 'Escape') close();
    e.stopPropagation(); e.preventDefault();
  }, true);

  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var a = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('.look a, .lookup a, a.zm-link');
    if (!a) return;
    var id = (a.getAttribute('href') || '').replace(/^#\//, '');
    if (REF.indexOf(id) < 0) return;
    e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation();
    open(id);
  }, true);

  function sync() {
    var cur = Reveal.getCurrentSlide();
    backBtn.classList.toggle('show', !!cur && REF.indexOf(cur.id) >= 0);
    if (zm.classList.contains('open')) close();
  }
  function init() { build(); Reveal.on('slidechanged', sync); sync(); }
  if (window.Reveal && Reveal.isReady && Reveal.isReady()) init();
  else window.addEventListener('load', function () { if (Reveal.isReady()) init(); else Reveal.on('ready', init); });
})();
</script>
```

## Activities, Actors, Artefacts


<p class="lead">Most AI use today is a chat window next to a workflow that stays the same. This model starts from the workflow instead, and asks three things of every stage.</p>

```{=html}
<div class="cards c3">
  <div class="card"><span class="ct">Activities</span><span class="q">What happens, in what order?</span><span>Split the workflow into 5–7 stages, each a verb: pull, check, decide, draft, sign off.</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="ct">Actors</span><span class="q">Who does each stage?</span><span>You, colleagues, counterparts, or an agent. Mark each stage: <i>I am part of this</i>, or <i>it happens without me</i>.</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="ct">Artefacts</span><span class="q">What goes in, what comes out?</span><span>Each stage uses tools and inputs, and hands an output to the next stage: a file, a memo, a decision.</span></div>
</div>
<div class="contrast">
  <div class="old"><b>AI on the side</b>You still do every step yourself, and ask a chatbot for help along the way.</div>
  <div class="new"><b>Agent in the loop</b>The workflow is built around handoffs. The agent owns whole stages; you own the decisions between them.</div>
</div>
```

::: {.notes}
The concept behind the Q1 slide. Activities, Actors, Artefacts. The contrast at the bottom is the key idea: an agent that owns whole stages, with the person owning the decisions in between.

For each stage, ask: does it need my judgment, what does the agent hand back, and what starts it?
:::

## Anatomy of a workflow matrix: answering a ministry data request

```{=html}
<div class="a3wrap">
  <span class="mk m1 fragment"></span><span class="mk m2 fragment"></span><span class="mk m3 fragment"></span><span class="mk m4 fragment"></span><span class="mk m5 fragment"></span><span class="mk m6 fragment"></span>
  <div class="a3">
    <div class="sp"></div><div class="hd">Stage →</div>
    <div class="hd c1"><i>1</i>Request arrives</div><div class="hd c2"><i>2</i>Scope it</div><div class="hd c3"><i>3</i>Disclosure check</div><div class="hd c4"><i>4</i>Produce tables</div><div class="hd c5"><i>5</i>Package &amp; document</div><div class="hd c6"><i>6</i>Clear &amp; send</div>

    <div class="grp g1 r1" style="--span:3">Activities</div>
    <div class="rl r1">Activity</div>
    <div class="r1 c1">Ministry asks for attendance by district and gender</div><div class="r1 c2">Agree indicators, years, breakdowns, deadline</div><div class="r1 c3">Check the spec against the data-sharing agreement</div><div class="r1 c4">Agent writes the code; I review code and numbers</div><div class="r1 c5">Format tables, write notes on definitions and sample</div><div class="r1 c6">TTL clears the reply and sends it</div>
    <div class="rl r1">Where / when</div>
    <div class="r1 c1">Email, any day</div><div class="r1 c2">15-minute call</div><div class="r1 c3">Once the spec is agreed</div><div class="r1 c4">Same day</div><div class="r1 c5">When I ask, after my review</div><div class="r1 c6">Email, async</div>
    <div class="rl r1">Outcome</div>
    <div class="r1 c1">Request on our desk</div><div class="r1 c2">Everyone wants the same table</div><div class="r1 c3">Small cells and identifiers flagged</div><div class="r1 c4">Numbers I'd stand behind</div><div class="r1 c5">Readable without us in the room</div><div class="r1 c6">Request answered and logged</div>

    <div class="grp g2 r2" style="--span:2">Actors</div>
    <div class="rl r2">My role</div>
    <div class="r2 c1"><span class="role without">without me</span></div><div class="r2 c2"><span class="role with">I'm in it</span></div><div class="r2 c3"><span class="role without">without me</span></div><div class="r2 c4"><span class="role with">I'm in it</span></div><div class="r2 c5"><span class="role without">without me</span></div><div class="r2 c6"><span class="role without">without me</span></div>
    <div class="rl r2">Who</div>
    <div class="r2 c1"><span class="ch ppl">Ministry</span><span class="ch ppl">TTL</span></div>
    <div class="r2 c2"><span class="ch me">Me</span><span class="ch ppl">Ministry</span></div>
    <div class="r2 c3"><span class="ch agent">Agent</span></div>
    <div class="r2 c4"><span class="ch me">Me</span><span class="ch agent">Agent</span></div>
    <div class="r2 c5"><span class="ch agent">Agent</span></div>
    <div class="r2 c6"><span class="ch ppl">TTL</span></div>

    <div class="grp g3 r3" style="--span:2">Artefacts</div>
    <div class="rl r3">Tools in</div>
    <div class="r3 c1">Email</div><div class="r3 c2">Call, notes</div><div class="r3 c3">Agent, data agreement</div><div class="r3 c4">Agent, clean data, Git</div><div class="r3 c5">Agent, table template</div><div class="r3 c6">Email, request log</div>
    <div class="rl r3">Output</div>
    <div class="r3 c1"><span class="ch art">Request email</span></div><div class="r3 c2"><span class="ch art">Request spec</span></div><div class="r3 c3"><span class="ch art">Disclosure memo</span></div><div class="r3 c4"><span class="ch art">Tables</span><span class="ch art">Code</span></div><div class="r3 c5"><span class="ch art">Excel file</span><span class="ch art">Data note</span></div><div class="r3 c6"><span class="ch art">Sent reply</span><span class="ch art">Log entry</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="a3-note">
    <div class="n0">A ministry asks for attendance figures by district and gender. One column per stage, one row per question.</div>
    <div class="n1"><b>1 · Request arrives</b> Happens without me. The ministry and the TTL start it; the artefact is the request email.</div>
    <div class="n2"><b>2 · Scope it</b> I'm in it. A 15-minute call turns a vague ask into a spec everyone agrees on.</div>
    <div class="n3"><b>3 · Disclosure check</b> Runs without me. The agent checks the spec against the data agreement and hands back a memo.</div>
    <div class="n4"><b>4 · Produce tables</b> I'm in it. The agent writes the code; I own the numbers. Output: tables plus the code that made them.</div>
    <div class="n5"><b>5 · Package &amp; document</b> When I ask, after my review. The agent formats and documents, so the reply stands on its own.</div>
    <div class="n6"><b>6 · Clear &amp; send</b> Happens without me. The TTL clears and sends; the log entry closes the loop.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.notes}
Click through the six stages. For each, name Activities, Actors and Artefacts out loud: what happens, who is in it, what gets handed on.

Point out that only stages 2 and 4 need the economist. The agent runs 3 and 5 alone, and every agent stage ends in an artefact someone can check.
:::

```{=html}
        { n: 'Agree the brief', when: 'Call, 3 weeks out', role: 'with', who: [me(), p('TTL'), p('Ministry')],
          act: 'Agree the audience, the time slot, and the three questions the Ministry wants answered.',
          how: 'Everyone on the call. The counterpart decides what matters to them; I take notes.',
          tools: 'Video call, shared notes', outc: 'We know what the deck has to answer.', out: ['One-page brief'] },
        { n: 'Map the evidence', when: 'Once the brief is agreed', role: 'without', who: [ag()],
          act: 'Match each question to the tables and figures that answer it. List the gaps.',
          how: 'The agent reads the brief and the results repo. It never re-estimates anything.',
          tools: 'Results repo, past mission notes', outc: 'Every question has evidence, or a flagged gap.', out: ['Evidence map'] },
        { n: 'Write the storyline', when: '1 hour', role: 'with', who: [me(), ag()],
          act: 'Pick the three messages, and the one exhibit that carries each.',
          how: 'The agent proposes messages in plain language. I rewrite them and choose the exhibits.',
          tools: 'Evidence map, agent', outc: 'A storyline the TTL would sign.', out: ['Storyline'] },
        { n: 'Build the deck', when: 'When I ask; runs while I do other work', role: 'without', who: [ag()],
          act: 'Build slides from the template, redraw charts with plain labels, add speaker notes and a handout.',
          how: 'Works only from the storyline and the repo, so every chart traces back to code.',
          tools: 'Deck template, plotting code', outc: 'A complete draft deck.', out: ['Draft deck', 'Handout'] },
        { n: 'Check every claim', when: 'Right after stage 4', role: 'without', who: [ag()],
          act: 'Check every number against the results tables. Flag claims stronger than the evidence.',
          how: 'Runs without me. It flags, it does not edit.',
          tools: 'Results tables, draft deck', outc: 'Numbers match; causal language checked.', out: ['Check report'] },
        { n: 'Rehearse & finalise', when: 'Week before', role: 'with', who: [me(), p('TTL'), ag()],
          act: 'Fix the flags, do a dry run with the TTL, prepare for the hard questions.',
          how: 'The agent drafts the ten questions the Ministry is most likely to ask; we practise answers.',
          tools: 'Check report, dry run', outc: 'Ready for the room.', out: ['Final deck', 'Q&A sheet'] }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'Cleaning a survey round',
      sub: 'Weekly batches from a phone survey, run by a survey firm',
      tag: 'The agent never touches raw data and never decides what counts as an error. It finds, records and rebuilds.',
      stages: [
        { n: 'Batch arrives', when: 'Every Monday', role: 'without', who: [p('Survey firm')],
          act: "The survey firm uploads the week's interviews.",
          how: 'Their own process. Encrypted upload to the project server.',
          tools: 'Survey server', outc: 'Raw data is on the server.', out: ['Raw batch'] },
        { n: 'Run checks', when: 'When the batch lands, I ask', role: 'without', who: [ag()],
          act: 'High-frequency checks: duplicates, outliers, skip logic, interview length, enumerator patterns.',
          how: 'Runs without me. Raw data is read-only.',
          tools: 'Check scripts, agent', outc: 'Every problem listed, with its ID.', out: ['Flag list', 'Check report'] },
        { n: 'Triage flags', when: 'Monday, 1 hour', role: 'with', who: [me(), ag()],
          act: 'Sort each flag: real error, plausible, or ask the field team.',
          how: 'The agent proposes a category and a reason for each flag. I decide.',
          tools: 'Flag list', outc: 'A clear instruction for every flag.', out: ['Decision log'] },
        { n: 'Field follow-up', when: 'Tuesday to Thursday', role: 'without', who: [p('Field coordinator'), p('Survey firm')],
          act: 'Call back respondents and enumerators about the open queries.',
          how: 'The field team records answers in the tracking sheet.',
          tools: 'Tracking sheet, phone', outc: 'Open queries are resolved.', out: ['Resolved queries'] },
        { n: 'Apply corrections', when: 'Once the sheet is filled in', role: 'without', who: [ag()],
          act: 'Write each correction into the cleaning script, rerun the pipeline, update the codebook.',
          how: 'Corrections live in code, never in the raw data.',
          tools: 'Cleaning script, Git', outc: 'Clean data that can be rebuilt from raw.', out: ['Clean data', 'Changelog'] },
        { n: 'Approve & lock', when: 'Friday', role: 'with', who: [me()],
          act: 'Review the changelog, spot-check ten records, tag the version.',
          how: 'Nothing reaches the analysis folder without my tag.',
          tools: 'Changelog, Git', outc: 'A versioned dataset the team can trust.', out: ['Tagged release'] }
      ]
    }
  ];

  var PER = 7;                       // overview + 6 stages
  var TOTAL = EX.length * PER;       // states 0 .. TOTAL-1
  var root = document.getElementById('x3');
  var marks = root.querySelector('.x3-marks');
  var tabs = root.querySelectorAll('.x3-tab');
  var subEl = root.querySelector('.x3-sub');
  var grid = root.querySelector('.x3-grid');
  var detail = root.querySelector('.x3-detail');
  var dots = root.querySelector('.x3-dots');
  var shownE = -1, shownS = -1;

  for (var i = 0; i < TOTAL - 1; i++) {
    var m = document.createElement('span');
    m.className = 'mk fragment';
    m.setAttribute('data-fragment-index', i);
    marks.appendChild(m);
  }
  for (var d = 0; d < PER; d++) dots.appendChild(document.createElement('span'));

  function chip(a) {
    return '<span class="ch ' + a.t + '">' + (a.t === 'agent' ? ICON_AGENT : '') + a.n + '</span>';
  }
  function roleBadge(r) {
    return r === 'with' ? '<span class="role with">I\'m in it</span>' : '<span class="role without">without me</span>';
  }

  function buildGrid(e) {
    var st = EX[e].stages, h = '';
    var rows = [['h', 'Stage'], ['r', 'My role'], ['w', 'Who'], ['o', 'Output']];
    rows.forEach(function (row) {
      h += '<div class="x3-lab">' + row[1] + '</div>';
      st.forEach(function (s, k) {
        var agentOnly = s.who.length === 1 && s.who[0].t === 'agent';
        var cls = 'x3-cell ' + row[0] + (agentOnly ? ' ag' : '') + (row[0] === 'o' && k === st.length - 1 ? ' last' : '');
        var inner = '';
        if (row[0] === 'h') inner = '<span><i>' + (k + 1) + '</i> ' + s.n + '</span><small>' + s.when + '</small>';
        if (row[0] === 'r') inner = roleBadge(s.role);
        if (row[0] === 'w') inner = s.who.map(chip).join('');
        if (row[0] === 'o') inner = s.out.map(function (o) { return '<span class="ch art">' + o + '</span>'; }).join('');
        h += '<div class="' + cls + '" data-k="' + k + '">' + inner + '</div>';
      });
    });
    grid.innerHTML = h;
    grid.querySelectorAll('.x3-cell').forEach(function (c) {
      c.addEventListener('click', function () { go(e * PER + 1 + (+c.getAttribute('data-k'))); });
    });
    subEl.innerHTML = '<b>' + EX[e].title + ':</b> ' + EX[e].sub;
  }

  function paneHTML(e, s) {
    var ex = EX[e];
    if (s === 0) {
      var w = ex.stages.filter(function (x) { return x.role === 'with'; }).length;
      var a = ex.stages.filter(function (x) { return x.who.some(function (y) { return y.t === 'agent'; }); }).length;
      return '<div class="x3-pane ov"><div class="tag">' + ex.tag + '</div>' +
        '<div class="legend"><div>' + chip(me()) + ' you</div><div>' + chip(ag()) + ' runs a whole stage</div><div>' + chip(p('Colleague')) + ' other people</div></div>' +
        '<div class="count">You are in <b>' + w + ' of 6</b> stages. The agent works in <b>' + a + '</b>, and runs ' +
        ex.stages.filter(function (x) { return x.who.length === 1 && x.who[0].t === 'agent'; }).length + ' of them on its own.</div></div>';
    }
    var st = ex.stages[s - 1];
    return '<div class="x3-pane"><div class="nm"><span class="big">' + s + '</span><span class="t">' + st.n + '</span>' +
      '<span>' + roleBadge(st.role) + '</span><span style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:4px">' + st.who.map(chip).join('') + '</span></div>' +
      '<div class="f"><b>Activity</b>' + st.act + '</div><div class="f"><b>How</b>' + st.how + '</div>' +
      '<div class="f"><b>Tools in</b>' + st.tools + '</div><div class="f"><b>Outcome</b>' + st.outc + '</div></div>';
  }

  function render(state) {
    var e = Math.floor(state / PER), s = state % PER;
    if (e === shownE && s === shownS) return;
    if (e !== shownE) buildGrid(e);
    tabs.forEach(function (t, k) { t.classList.toggle('on', k === e); });
    root.classList.toggle('focus', s > 0);
    grid.querySelectorAll('.x3-cell').forEach(function (c) { c.classList.toggle('cur', +c.getAttribute('data-k') === s - 1); });
    dots.querySelectorAll('span').forEach(function (dd, k) { dd.classList.toggle('on', k === s); });
    detail.querySelectorAll('.x3-pane').forEach(function (old) {
      old.classList.add('out');
      setTimeout(function () { old.remove(); }, 260);
    });
    detail.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', paneHTML(e, s));
    shownE = e; shownS = s;
  }

  function slideEl() { return root.closest('section'); }
  function currentState() { return slideEl().querySelectorAll('.x3-marks .fragment.visible').length; }
  function go(state) {
    var idx = Reveal.getIndices(slideEl());
    Reveal.slide(idx.h, idx.v, state - 1);
  }

  tabs.forEach(function (t) {
    t.addEventListener('click', function () { go(+t.getAttribute('data-e') * PER); });
  });

  function sync() { render(currentState()); }
  function init() {
    ['slidechanged', 'fragmentshown', 'fragmenthidden', 'ready'].forEach(function (ev) { Reveal.on(ev, sync); });
    sync();
  }
  render(0);
  if (window.Reveal && Reveal.isReady && Reveal.isReady()) init();
  else window.addEventListener('load', function () { if (window.Reveal) { if (Reveal.isReady()) init(); else Reveal.on('ready', init); } });
})();
</script>
```

::: {.notes}
Use the arrow keys or clicker: each example opens on an overview, then steps through its six stages. Click a tab to jump to an example, or a column to jump to a stage.

Ask the room which of the three is closest to a workflow in their own project. That workflow is a good candidate for section 2 of the plan.
:::

## Example: an AI data map {.smaller}

| Stage | AI task | Data in | Classification | Data out | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Design** | Literature search, concept note feedback | Concept note, published papers | Official Use Only | Summary, cited sources | PI verifies every citation |
| **Acquisition** | Program survey form, translate questions | Questionnaire, codebook | Official Use Only | Form code, translations | Field team pilots, local-language review |
| **Processing** | Write and review cleaning code | Code, variable names, **synthetic** data | Official Use Only | Cleaning scripts | RA compares counts before and after |
| **Analysis** | Write and review analysis code, exhibits | Code, **de-identified** data | Confidential | Tables, figures | Analyst inspects every exhibit |
| **Publication** | Slides, brief, reproducibility package | Paper draft, exhibits | Official Use Only | Drafts, package | Author owns every claim; AI use disclosed |

::: {.notes}
Illustrative only. Classifications depend on the project's data agreements. Emphasize that identified data does not appear in the "data in" column at any stage.
:::

## Example: an AI data map for a dashboard {.smaller}

Many teams work like this: data arrives in Excel files and PDF reports, gets analysed, and ends up in a dashboard.

| Stage | AI task | Data in | Classification | Data out | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Collect** | Extract tables from Excel files and PDF reports into one format | Excel files, PDF reports | Depends on source: often Official Use Only | One combined dataset, extraction log | Analyst spot-checks against the source files |
| **Clean** | Write cleaning and validation code; flag inconsistencies | Combined dataset, codebook | Same as source | Clean dataset, issue list | Analyst reviews every flag |
| **Analyse** | Write code for the indicators | Clean dataset | Same as source | Indicator tables | Analyst compares with the last update |
| **Dashboard** | Build or update the dashboard code | Indicator tables | Same as source | Updated dashboard | Team lead reviews before sharing |
| **Share** | Draft a short note on what changed | Indicator tables, dashboard | Official Use Only | Draft note | Author owns every claim |

::: {.notes}
Added because many participants' projects look like this rather than a classic research pipeline. Classifications are illustrative: they follow the source files. If a source has personal or restricted data, it needs a plan first (see "Prepare sensitive data").
:::

## Plan your tasks {#plan-your-tasks}

Sort each task in your plan by how ready it is. The examples are illustrations, not a checklist.

| When | Tasks that fit here | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Now** (this week) | Already work, low risk | Adjust your memory file to your real project; use the agent on one recurring task, such as cleaning code, a monthly update or a data request |
| **Next 6 weeks** | Need some setup or team agreement | A de-identified or synthetic version of sensitive data; AI review as a routine step; team members onboarded |
| **Next 3 months** | Not plug-and-play yet: start defining the need now | Review and quality-control routines; one workflow redesigned end to end; a reproducibility package for a paper |

::: {.notes}
This slide should explain itself: people read it during the hands-on. The 6-week and 3-month targets are the ones in the follow-up survey. A few specific targets beat many general ones.
:::

## Which skills does your project need? {#skills}

```{=html}
<div class="cards c3 sk">
  <div class="card"><span class="num">1</span><span class="ct">Find the tasks</span>
    <span>Look for repetitive, structured tasks in your work: the same steps every time, and a clear idea of what a good result looks like.</span></div>
  <div class="card"><span class="num">2</span><span class="ct">Check existing skills</span>
    <span>Some are covered by skills from this week:</span>
    <ul><li>Code review</li><li>Reproducible charts and tables</li><li>Presentations</li><li>Working-paper feedback</li><li>Reproducibility packages</li></ul></div>
  <div class="card road"><span class="num">3</span><span class="ct">Note what is missing</span>
    <span>No skill yet? Write down the task, how often it recurs, and what a good result looks like. Add it to your roadblocks and tell us: it helps us plan a follow-on session on building skills.</span></div>
</div>
```

::: {.notes}
Start from tasks, not from skills. We did not teach skill-building this week, so do not suggest that people write their own yet; collect the missing ones.
:::

## Who needs access, and to what?

AI adoption fails when only one person on the team uses the tools. For each team member, write down:

| Team member | Role | Responsible for | Needs access to | Needs training on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Name* | Team lead | Reviewing and signing off outputs | Approved chat tool | Ethics, verifying AI outputs |
| *Name* | Analyst or RA | Cleaning and analysis code, dashboards | Coding agent, GitHub repository | Memory files, skills, code review |
| *Name* | Field or operations coordinator | Data collection, partner communication | Approved chat tool | Data classification |

::: {.notes}
"Responsible for" is what the person does in the workflow; "Needs training on" is what they still need to learn to do it with AI. Not everyone needs a coding agent. Everyone who handles sensitive data needs the data classification rules from Day 1.
:::

## Prepare sensitive data before the agent sees it {#sensitive-data}

**Public and non-sensitive data can live in your project folder.** Sensitive data, such as personal information, confidential documents or restricted government data, needs a plan **before** the agent works on that step:

- **De-identify.** Run a de-identification script on the raw data, outside any AI tool.
- **Use synthetic data.** If you cannot de-identify safely, generate a synthetic dataset with the same structure, so the agent can write and test code against it.
- **Keep it away from the agent.** Store it outside your project folder, or in folders blocked in the agent's permission settings.

::: {.callout-note-custom}
De-identification is a human responsibility. An agent can help write the script from the codebook, but it should never see the sensitive data while doing so.
:::

::: {.notes}
Credit: suggestion from Ankriti Singh.

Removing names alone does not make a dataset safe to share (see Day 1 ethics session). Indirect identifiers such as village, exact dates and rare combinations of characteristics matter too.

Listing allowed and forbidden folders in the memory file is an optional extra; the guide has a short example. Permission settings are what actually enforce it.
:::

## Risks and how to reduce them

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Sensitive data reaches an AI tool | Classify first; de-identified or synthetic versions; sensitive data outside the project folder or in blocked folders |
| AI output is wrong but looks right | Human review of every exhibit and number; Git diffs to see what changed |
| Only one person uses the tools | Shared memory file and skills in the project folder; onboarding target in the plan |
| Costs or token limits run out | Use cheaper models for routine tasks (Day 1 cost session) |
| AI use is not documented | Record AI use in commits and in the reproducibility package; disclose meaningful assistance |
| The plan is forgotten | Save the plan in your project folder; follow-up survey on the 6-week targets |

::: {.notes}
Ask participants to add at least one risk that is specific to their project, for example a data agreement that restricts processing by third parties.
:::
